slides.heading: GROWTH, FY23 → FY25 (%)
slides.body: Payouts grew four to five times faster than premium.

slides.heading: PRIVATE LIFE INSURERS' EXPENSES
slides.body: Down from 21.3% in FY15, then back up after the 2023 reforms removed commission caps.

slides.heading: WHAT IRDAI PROPOSES
items: NO SALES INCENTIVES FOR BANK STAFF

slides.heading: CAPS FOR BROKERS, BANKS, AGGREGATORS (%)
slides.body: Agents get higher caps. Sales tied to a loan get lower ones.

slides.heading: BANKS
slides.text: “prohibit any volume linked or reward linked incentive for bank or NBFC staff selling insurance”

slides.heading: COMMISSION, % OF PREMIUM · FY26
slides.body: The cheapest sellers are already inside the proposed limits.

slides.heading: THE MOAT QUESTION
slides.label: FOCUS MOAT · D3 COST ADVANTAGE
slides.body: For insurers that already sell cheaply, the reform is not a cost. It is a constraint on their competitors.

slides.heading: THE BEAR CASE
items: IT IS A DRAFT: COMMENTS TILL 25 OCT
LOWER COMMISSIONS MAY MEAN LOWER SALES
BANKS MAY RESTRUCTURE HOW THEY ARE PAID

sources: IRDAI, Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution
Public consultation paper, Parts 1 and 2, 23 Sep 2026
